Messages.Author: Joshua Duffin
Messages.Body:
Beatrice Tremblay says: "During your untap phase, another ready imbued
you control takes 1 unpreventable damage. +1 bleed."

Does "another ready Imbued" mean that if she is *not* ready, the damage
will not be inflicted?

I think the damage is still inflicted and doesn't care if she's become
unready, but maybe the phrase should apply to both ends of the ability...

Josh

ask another ready judge

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <4f0krmF...@individual.net>, Joshua Duffin

<jtdu...@yahoo.com> writes:
>Beatrice Tremblay says: "During your untap phase, another ready imbued
>you control takes 1 unpreventable damage. +1 bleed."
>
>Does "another ready Imbued" mean that if she is *not* ready, the damage
>will not be inflicted?

Alexandra sets precedent on this. There "another ready Toreador" means
"another Toreador, i.e. not Alexandra, who is ready" and not "both
Alexandra and some other Toreador, who are both ready." And Alexandra
can untap other vampires while in torpor herself.

e.g. a ruling at <http://groups.google.com/group/rec.games.trading-
cards.jyhad/msg/39e639f75959bc73> shows Alexandra can untap others while
in torpor herself. Alexandra's card text:

"Once during your turn, you may tap or untap another ready Toreador. +2
bleed."

By extension this would be read as "another Imbued, i.e. not Beatrice,
who is ready."

--
